newsitem.title: EGYPT: Two dead, 100 missing as Cairo building crumbles.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 100 missing as Cairo building crumbles.

text.p: Two people were killed and at least 100 others are feared dead after an 11-storey residential building collapsed in a mountain of rubble in a Cairo suburb on Sunday.

Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told Reuters that rescue workers had so far pulled out 19 survivors and were franctically searching beneath the concrete slabs and metal girders for more people.
"It is too early to tell the cause of the collapse... what we are working on now is getting as many alive people as possible," he said.

Doctor Tala'at Ezzedine of the nearby Manshiyet Bakry hospital said rescue crews had found 17 people in the rubble. He said two of the people later died and that the other 15 were being treated for injuries.
Only a corner of the 25-year-old apartment block remained standing and a policeman at the scene said rescue workers thought this is where any survivors were likely to be.
"There is a possibility that there are still people alive, this corner is upright and I believe people are in there," he told Reuters as rescue workers used bulldozers to dig beneath the rubble.
The building is located in Heliopolis suburb, two blocks away from the residence of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"Noura, Noura my daughter, Noura," wailed an elderly woman in a black robe. Others shouted the names of relatives while some sobbed hysterically outside the cordoned-off area.
"All of a sudden we heard a sound like a bomb and then dust. Then we heard what sounded like people crying for help," said Magdi Abdel Fouttouh who lives in the neighbouring block.
The porter of the building said he thought renovation work in one of the 40 apartments might have affected the infrastructure and caused the collapse.
Residents of the area said the landlord had erected seven illegal floors and that the local council had been demanding their removal since 1991.
Abdel Fouttouh said he thought a bank had set up in one of the building's floors and was renovating. "They may have removed some columns on the inside," he said.
Passers-by helped rescue workers mine the rubble mountain, pulling out an empty car and crushed refrigerators.
Doctor Mahmoud Riyad of Manshiet el-Bakry hospital said one of the dead was an old woman who had suffocated beneath the dust and concrete slabs.
Soaring real estate prices have often pushed landlords to add extra floors on top of their property, usually illegally.
Several buildings have collapsed beneath the extra weight and recent earthquake have also taken their toll on poorly constructed buildings in the crowded capital.
Ganzouri said the collapse took place at about 8 pm local time (1800 GMT) but eyewitnesses said it fell a few hours earlier.
